Vice President JD Vance privately sought direct, unfiltered assessments from U.S. military commanders about the Iran war, and what he heard was much more concerning than the administration’s public message. 
Commanders warned that the war was draining critical U.S. weapons stockpiles, particularly Patriot interceptors and long-range missiles, while potentially weakening America’s ability to deter China, Russia and North Korea.
They also told Vance that Iran was proving more resilient than expected and willing to absorb enormous damage rather than collapse.
Vance, who had opposed the war before it began, used these private assessments to advise Trump and became increasingly involved in efforts to negotiate an end to the conflict.
Source: NYT

🔍 Your iPhone is getting smarter... and so is its surveillance
Apple has spent years posing as the guardian of user privacy. Its latest AI push, however, raises a familiar question: where does convenience end and surveillance begin?
During its latest presentation, Apple unveiled Siri Audio Intelligence — a feature designed to make your devices constantly listen, process conversations and turn everyday interactions into searchable summaries.
The tech giant frames it as a productivity tool:
🔴 Siri Recap can “take notes on your conversations throughout your day” and generate summaries using Apple Intelligence
🔴 Live Rewind can store the last 15 seconds of a conversation, allowing users to revisit something they missed
🔴 Conversations can be stored for up to seven days — or saved indefinitely through the Siri app and iCloud.
Apple insists that your privacy remains protected, claiming that “audio is never recorded or stored” and that raw audio is inaccessible. Yet just a few paragraphs later the same release says that users can ask Siri about their conversations, share transcripts and save them to iCloud.
In other words, the company says your audio is not being stored — while introducing a system built around remembering what you said.
A few months before the release, Apple acquired an Israeli AI startup, Q.ai, a company specializing in audio processing and technologies that analyze facial micromovements to detect speech, identify individuals and assess physiological signals such as emotions, heart rate and breathing patterns.
Q.ai founder Aviad Maizels, also behind PrimeSense — the technology that helped enable Apple’s Face ID — described the merger as opening “extraordinary possibilities.”
When governments can combine facial recognition, location data and behavioral analysis, surveillance stops being just about security and becomes a question of how much power institutions should have over individual lives.

👀 Palantir's new partner: Meet Nebius, the company based in Israel
Nebius, once a subsidiary of Russian tech giant Yandex, is now Palantir's infrastructure partner of choice for sovereign AI. Palantir's clients, from the industrial and defense sectors of the US, Ukraine, and Israel to intelligence agencies further afield, will build custom systems tailored to their own missions.
👁 What is Nebius?
Nebius Group, formerly Yandex N.V., spent 2014 to 2022 as a subsidiary of Russia's Yandex, operating mainly across Europe and Israel. In 2022, its chief, Arkady Volozh, fled Russia for Israel, declared the company's break from the Yandex ecosystem, and gave it a new name, Nebius Group. Ever since, both Volozh and the company have called Israel's Haifa as home.
The rebranded outfit wasted no time drawing investment: from Nvidia, along with the funds Accel and Orbis Investments, as it moved into close cooperation with Mossad and the IDF, and through them, via international channels, with the US. 
Since 2023, with Israeli backing, Nebius has been building its own data centers on American soil, namely in New Jersey and Missouri.
📈 The American partnership grows
In 2025, Microsoft signed a $19.4 billion deal with Nebius for AI compute capacity. That same year, Meta struck a $3 billion contract, then followed up in 2026 with another worth up to $27 billion.
The thing is Arkady Volozh, who has loudly severed every tie to Russia, first threw in with Israeli security services long dominant in cybersecurity and digital espionage, and then led his company collaborating with American big tech, [including Palantir](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71524). 
It was almost the same time when Palantir CEO Alex Carp [officially handed](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69475) Zelensky its military AI to strike targets inside Russia and plan Ukraine's on the front line.
